issue.title: Feature - Workflow for automating deployments to Netlify
issue.body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a GitHub Actions workflow to build and deploy the Compose Web sample app to Netlify.

[![Preview Screenshot](https://i9.ytimg.com/vi/sJio81gll8U/mqdefault.jpg?sqp=CMjq6c0G-oaymwEmCMACELQB8quKqQMa8AEB-AH-CYACzAWKAgwIABABGGUgZShlMA8=&rs=AOn4CLC_LAJYqaA9qFIiLgaRaM7cg1HcCg)](https://youtu.be/sJio81gll8U)

## Changes
- Added workflow file `.github/workflows/deploy-netlify.yml`
- Configured release event trigger (`on: release: types: [published]`)
- Set `production-deploy: true` to push directly to production
- Secured Netlify credentials via GitHub secrets (`NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `NETLIFY_SITE_ID`)

## Netlify Setup
- Get OAuth from User settings 
- Get Project Id / Site Id 
- Add both as Secrets in GitHub settings

## Testing
- Verified successful deploy on release event
- Confirmed production site updates correctly
- [Live Test Site](https://calf-webapp.netlify.app)

BREAKING

  • Removed support for Dokka v1, it's now required to use Dokka in v2 mode.
  • Mark DirectorySignatureType internal.

Behavior changes

  • validateDeployment now has the DeploymentValidation enum as type instead of being a boolean. The default is now to just wait for the VALIDATED state. The previous behavior can be achieved by setting it to PUBLISHED. NONE can be used for disabling the validation completely.
  • When calling configure(...) manually to configure what to publish and not passing javadocJar explicity, the plugin now defaults to publishing an empty javadoc jar.

Features

  • Android projects now support using Dokka for javadoc creation, this will happen automatically when using the default options and the Dokka plugin is applied to the project.
  • Added consistent JavadocJar and SourcesJar options to configureBasedOnAppliedPlugins and to all applicable project types that can be passed to configure. The previous Boolean based versions have been deprecated.
  • When enabling Maven Central publishing through the DSL, the mavenCentralDeploymentValidation and mavenCentralAutomaticPublishing are used for the default values of the 2 parameters when they are not passed explicitly. This allows to more easily override them in certain environments.
  • When isolated projects is enabled the module/project specific gradle.properties files are now considered in the same way they are when isolated projects is disabled.

Improvements

  • Better error message when Maven Central credentials are missing.

0.36.0 (2026-01-13)

BREAKING

  • Updated minimum supported JDK, Gradle, Android Gradle Plugin and Kotlin versions.
  • Removed support for Dokka v1, it's now required to use Dokka in v2 mode.
  • Mark DirectorySignatureType internal.

Behavior changes

  • validateDeployment now has the DeploymentValidation enum as type instead of being a boolean. The default is now to just wait for the VALIDATED state. The previous behavior can be achieved by setting it to PUBLISHED. NONE can be used for disabling the validation completely.
  • When calling configure(...) manually to configure what to publish and not passing javadocJar explicity, the plugin now defaults to publishing an empty javadoc jar.

Features

  • Android projects now support using Dokka for javadoc creation, this will happen automatically when using the default options and the Dokka plugin is applied to the project.
  • Added consistent JavadocJar and SourcesJar options to configureBasedOnAppliedPlugins and to all applicable project types that can be passed to configure. The previous Boolean based versions have been deprecated.
  • When enabling Maven Central publishing through the DSL, the mavenCentralDeploymentValidation and mavenCentralAutomaticPublishing are used for the default values of the 2 parameters when they are not passed explicitly. This allows to more easily override them in certain environments.
  • When isolated projects is enabled the module/project specific gradle.properties files are now considered in the same way they are when isolated projects is disabled.

Improvements

  • Better error message when Maven Central credentials are missing.

issue.title: [Crash] [iOS only] When opening the screen which uses Calf UI Date Picker crashes
issue.body:
I'm experiencing critical iOS build and runtime issues with Calf v0.8.0 when using it in a Kotlin Multiplatform project. The issue manifests differently depending on the version combination:

1. **With Compose Multiplatform 1.8.2**: iOS build fails with IR lowering compilation error
2. **With Compose Multiplatform 1.9.0-rc02**: Build succeeds but app crashes at runtime when opening screens with Calf DatePicker

  ## Environment

- **Calf version**: 0.8.0
- **Kotlin version**: 2.2.0
- **KSP version**: 2.2.0-2.0.2
- **Target platforms**: Android, iOS, Desktop
- **iOS SDK**: 18.0
- **Xcode**: 16.0

## Reproduction Steps

### Scenario 1: Build Failure (Compose Multiplatform 1.8.2)

Using these versions in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`:
```
  [versions]
  kotlin = "2.2.0"
  composeMultiplatform = "1.8.2"
  navigationCompose = "2.9.0-beta02"
  calfUi = "0.8.0"

  Result: iOS build fails with:
  Compilation failed: IR lowering failed at: CurrencySelectionBottomSheet.kt
  java.lang.Exception: IR lowering failed at: CurrencySelectionBottomSheet.kt
  Compilation finished with errors
```

### Scenario 2: Runtime Crash (Compose Multiplatform 1.9.0-rc02)

Using these versions:
```
  [versions]
  kotlin = "2.2.0"
  composeMultiplatform = "1.9.0-rc02"
  navigationCompose = "2.9.0-beta03"
  calfUi = "0.8.0"
```

Result:
- iOS build succeeds ✅
- App crashes when navigating to any screen containing Calf DatePicker component ❌

Code Sample
```
The failing component uses Calf DatePicker in a bottom sheet:
  // CurrencySelectionBottomSheet.kt
  @Composable
  fun CurrencySelectionBottomSheet(
      // ... parameters
  ) {
      // Bottom sheet containing Calf UI components
      AdaptiveDatePicker(
          // ... configuration
      )
  }

  Build Configuration

  // build.gradle.kts (composeApp module)
  kotlin {
      listOf(
          iosX64(),
          iosArm64(),
          iosSimulatorArm64()
      ).forEach { iosTarget ->
          iosTarget.binaries.framework {
              baseName = "ComposeApp"
              isStatic = true
              export("com.mohamedrejeb.calf:calf-ui:0.8.0") // Properly exported as per docs
          }
      }

      sourceSets {
          commonMain.dependencies {
              api("com.mohamedrejeb.calf:calf-ui:0.8.0")
          }
      }
  }
```

  Expected Behavior

  The app should:
  1. Build successfully for iOS with Kotlin 2.2.0 and recent Compose Multiplatform versions
  2. Run without crashes when using Calf DatePicker components

  Actual Behavior

  - With Compose MP 1.8.2: Compilation fails with IR lowering error
  - With Compose MP 1.9.0-rc02: Runtime crash on DatePicker usage

  Additional Context

  - The issue only affects iOS; Android and Desktop targets work fine
  - All other non-Calf components work correctly
  - The framework is properly exported as per documentation

  Workaround Attempts

  1. ✅ Exporting calf-ui to iOS framework (already done)
  2. ❌ Trying different Compose Multiplatform versions (1.8.2 vs 1.9.0-rc02)
  3. ❌ Clean builds and pod cache clearing

  Questions

  1. Is Calf 0.8.0 compatible with Kotlin 2.2.0?
  2. Are there any known issues with Compose Multiplatform 1.9.0-rc02?

  This is blocking our iOS release. Any guidance would be greatly appreciated!
